speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show significant leukocytosis and a markedly elevated creatine kinase level of 5,600 U/L, suggesting severe muscle injury. Given your recent initiation or continued use of haloperidol, have you noticed any severe muscle rigidity, "cogwheel" stiffness, or a "lead-pipe" feeling in your limbs? Also, please tell me if you have experienced any visual disturbances or blurred vision.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and a significantly elevated creatine kinase (5,600 U/L) in a patient taking haloperidol is diagnostic for NMS. The normal deep tendon reflexes and preserved limb movement further support this over other etiologies like status epilepticus or toxic ingestion.
